settings.heading: Which joint runs your day?
settings.intro: Same wrap, different mornings. Tap the one that sounds like yours.
settings.cta_label: Try it on your worst joint
settings.footnote: Jointwell is a comfort device for stiff, tired joints. It is not a treatment for any condition and does not replace the care you are waiting for.

settings.title: The stiff knee at 7am
settings.line: The first ten steps are the worst. Then the kettle, then the stairs.
settings.panel_heading: The cold hour before the day starts
settings.text: Overnight a joint sits still and cools. The stiffness at 7am is a cold, unmoved knee, not the day getting worse. Kettle on, wrap on, level three, read the paper. By the second cup the wrap has clicked itself off and the knee has had thirty minutes of steady warmth before it is asked to do the stairs.
settings.fit: Straight round the knee, over pyjamas or trousers. One size, 55 cm strap span.
settings.alt: A man in his sixties at the kitchen table with tea and toast, wearing the wrap on his knee

settings.title: The shoulder that won't reach the top shelf
settings.line: Doing up a strap, lifting the kettle, sleeping on that side. Small things, twenty times a day.
settings.panel_heading: A shoulder is the hardest joint to keep warm
settings.text: A wheat bag slides off a shoulder. A hot water bottle needs the hand you wanted to use. Rubs reach the skin, not the joint. So the shoulder stays cold. Shoulder people tend to use the wrap twice: under a cardigan while the tea brews, and again in the armchair before bed. Being cordless is what makes the second one possible.
settings.fit: The extension strap in the box takes it from a knee loop to one that goes over the shoulder and under the arm, so the warm panel sits on the joint and stays there.
settings.alt: The wrap worn on a knee, a shoulder and an elbow, side by side

settings.title: The elbow that aches from the garden
settings.line: Secateurs, the watering can, forty years of one arm doing the work.
settings.text: Nobody over sixty got a bad elbow from tennis. It was the secateurs, the heavy watering can, the wallpaper stripping. The ache sits on the outside of the elbow and shows up when you grip, lift or turn a stiff tap. Half an hour of warmth in the chair, before the crossword or after the garden, is the routine people tell us about.
settings.fit: The extension strap runs the wrap up the forearm so it sits over the elbow. 360 g, so it does not drag.
settings.alt: A man doing the crossword in an armchair, wearing the wrap on his elbow

settings.title: The warm half hour before physio exercises
settings.line: Once your surgeon and physio say heat is fine, this is the bit before the work.
settings.text: Physiotherapists warm a joint before they work on it. If you have been given exercises to do at home, the same order applies: thirty minutes of steady warmth, then the sheet of exercises. Ask your surgeon or physio before using heat on a joint that has been operated on, and follow what they say over anything written here.
settings.fit: Round the knee while you sit up in bed or on the sofa, then off, then the exercises. It switches itself off at thirty minutes so it cannot be left running.
settings.alt: A woman reading in bed with the wrap on her knee

settings.title: The first ten steps of the day
settings.line: Kettle on, wrap on, before the stairs.
settings.text: Most people put it on with the first cup of tea and forget about it. It is light enough to walk to the kettle in. Thirty minutes later it clicks off, and the joint has had steady warmth rather than ten hot minutes and twenty lukewarm ones. A routine kept twice a week does nothing. Every morning is the point.
settings.fit: Strap on, press once, pick a level from 45°C. Big lit digits, no menus, no app.
settings.alt: A woman at the kettle in a cardigan and slippers, wearing the wrap on her knee

settings.title: Down to the flower beds and back up again
settings.line: Before you go out, and after you come in.
settings.panel_heading: Kneeling is the price of a garden
settings.text: Gardeners kneel, and kneeling is what a stiff knee hates most. People tell us they wear the wrap at the table before they go out, so the knee is warm when it first bends, and again when they come in with the mud still on their boots. It goes over trousers.
settings.fit: Over trousers, either knee. If both knees complain, two wraps at once is why the pair is the most chosen pack.
settings.alt: A woman sitting by the garden door with a cup of tea, wearing the wrap on her knee, raised beds behind her

settings.title: When the damp comes in
settings.line: October to March, and the van step at seven in the morning.
settings.panel_heading: One warm thing when everything else is cold
settings.text: The first cold snap is when most people go looking. Cold tightens everything around a joint, and a day on hard floors or a cold van seat finishes the job. The wrap runs off a battery, so it goes on in the van, in the caravan, or in the chair before the heating has caught up. One warm joint is not a substitute for a warm home. It is the thing you can do about the knee while the house catches up.
settings.fit: Cordless, so it goes wherever you are sitting. About four half-hour sessions per charge, off a phone charger.
settings.alt: A tradesman in a hi-vis jacket sitting on the step of his van, wearing the wrap on his knee

settings.heading: We are the ones selling it. So don't take our word for any of it.

settings.text: Boil your own hot water bottle. Put a hand on it after twenty minutes and again after thirty. You will not need us to tell you what you find.
Our CE test document is linked here. It covers electrical safety. It does not say this is a medical device, and we are not going to imply that it does.
Read the policy. We pay the postage back. A company that expected most people to send it back could not afford to write that.

Every one is from a customer with an order on file, in their own words, with the photo they sent us. We do not edit them, and the one who says the strap takes a minute to get right is on the page too.

settings.question: Isn't this just a heating pad with extra steps?
settings.answer: A heating pad gives you heat that fades, or heat that ties you to a wall socket. Jointwell holds whichever of the five levels you pick, 45°C to 65°C, for a full 30 minutes. It adds vibration massage at three strengths, straps on so it stays put, and runs cordless in any chair in the house.

settings.question: Will it work for me? My joints have been like this a long time.
settings.answer: It isn't a cure and we won't pretend otherwise. Nobody can promise what it will do for your joint. What we can promise is warmth at the level you choose, held for thirty minutes, with massage alongside it. The 90-day trial is there so your own knee gets the deciding vote rather than our copy.

settings.question: Will it fit me?
settings.answer: One size, 46 cm across and 30 cm tall, with a 55 cm strap span. It fits either knee, and the extension strap in the box takes it round a shoulder or up an arm to the elbow. If it doesn't fit you, the 90-day trial covers a full refund and we pay the return postage.

settings.question: Is it safe? Will it burn me?
settings.answer: You choose the heat level, from a gentle 45°C up to 65°C, and every session shuts off after 30 minutes, so it cannot be left running. Do not use it while asleep. If you have diabetes, circulation problems or reduced skin sensation, check with your GP before using any heat product.

settings.question: When will it arrive?
settings.answer: We dispatch within 1 to 3 working days and most orders arrive within 7 to 10 working days of ordering, occasionally up to 14. Every order is tracked and we email you the link the moment it leaves us.

settings.question: How do I know this isn't another Facebook gadget?
settings.answer: Fair question, because this market is full of them. We dispatch most orders within 1 to 3 working days and track every one. There's a UK returns address, UK support, a 2-year warranty, and a 90-day trial where we pay the postage back. The reviews on this page are from customers with an order on file, in their own words. Junk sellers can't afford the guarantee.

settings.question: Can I use it after a knee replacement?
settings.answer: Ask your surgeon or physio first, and follow what they say. Many people are told heat is fine once the wound has fully healed, but that is their call, not ours. If they say yes, most people use it as the warm half hour before their exercises.

settings.question: How do I charge it, and how long does a charge last?
settings.answer: It charges over USB-C with the cable in the box, the same cable as most phones. It has a 3000 mAh battery. The panel shows the battery level.

settings.question: What happens if I send it back?
settings.answer: Email us within 90 days of delivery. We send you a UK returns address and a postage label. Post it back, and we refund what you paid in full once it arrives. You do not pay the postage and you do not have to give a reason, though we would like to hear it.

settings.question: Who shouldn't use it?
settings.answer: Anyone who has been told to avoid heat on that joint. If you have diabetes, circulation problems, reduced feeling in your skin, a pacemaker, an unhealed wound or a joint that is hot, red and swollen, talk to your GP before using any heat product. Do not use it while asleep, over broken skin, or on a child. If you are pregnant or under medical care for the joint, ask first. It is a comfort device, not a treatment, and your GP's word beats ours.

settings.heading: What the NHS and orthopaedic surgeons say about heat and massage
settings.intro: None of these people are selling anything. These are their words about warmth and massage on stiff joints in general, with the source linked so you can read it yourself.
settings.evidence_note: Statements about heat in general, not about this device. Nothing here is a claim about what Jointwell will do for your joint.
settings.footnote: Jointwell is a comfort device. It is not a medical treatment and does not cure, treat or prevent any condition. Keep doing what your GP and physio have told you to do.

settings.role: nhs.uk, on easing joint stiffness at home
settings.quote: Heat applied to the affected area can be very effective in reducing pain.
Heat therapy is an easy, inexpensive, and medication-free way to relieve some types of arthritis stiffness and pain.

settings.role: Orthopaedic surgeon, hip and knee replacement
settings.quote: Using heat on sore or stiff joints can bring significant relief, especially when dealing with chronic arthritis pain.

settings.text: Heat-pack guidance says apply warmth for 15 to 20 minutes. A hot water bottle holds useful warmth for 20 to 30 minutes and a microwaved wheat bag about 30. The dose in your cupboard is roughly right. It is the delivery that runs out.
Knees, shoulders and elbows sit under thin skin with little muscle or fat around them, so they lose warmth faster than the rest of you and hold it worst. Cold hands, cold nose, cold knees.

NICE, which writes the guidance the NHS follows, puts exercise, weight management and information first for osteoarthritis. We are not a substitute for any of that. Warmth is what people use to get moving in the morning so they can do the rest.
settings.source: NICE guideline NG226, Osteoarthritis in over 16s (2022)
